diagnostic_evidence.quote: If moreover $\Omega$ is convex, then $\uu \in \WW$ with a bound

issues.failure_explanation: On nonconvex polygons, the variational Stokes domain need not require Δu∈L²: a singular pressure can cancel the non-L² part of Δu. For example, a 3π/2 corner admits clamped biharmonic modes ψ=r^(1+s)F(φ), with s∈(1/2,2/3) satisfying sin²(3πs/2)=s². After cutoff, u=Curl ψ belongs to V and −Δu+∇p belongs to L², whereas Δu behaves like r^(s−2) and is not in L². The stationary trajectory with this initial value satisfies the proposition's data assumptions, but A as defined cannot be applied to it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define D(A) as the variational operator domain: those u∈V for which there is F∈H satisfying (F,v)=(∇u,∇v) for every v∈V, and set Au=F. Do not infer unprojected-Laplacian regularity on nonconvex polygons.
issues.overall_effect: The nonconvex-domain maximal-regularity assertion is invalid with the stated domain of A.
issues.title: The Stokes regularity assertion uses an incorrectly restricted operator domain
issues.why_classification: The natural Stokes estimate survives through a contained domain correction, but the extra Δu∈L² regularity implicitly promised on nonconvex polygons must be withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Due to the regularity of $f$ and $\psi_0$, as a consequence of the interpolated regularity result in
    \Cref{corr:parabolic_regularity_interpolated}, we have

issues.failure_explanation: At θ=1/2, [H¹₀,H²₀]₁/₂ is the critical Lions–Magenes space, not ordinary H^(3/2)₀ defined by closure in the Sobolev norm. It includes an additional weighted boundary condition on the gradient. A smooth zero-trace function with nonzero normal derivative belongs to ordinary H^(3/2)₀ but fails that condition. Correspondingly, [H⁻²,H⁻¹]₁/₂ is the dual critical interpolation space, not the stated ordinary H^(−3/2). The endpoint estimates therefore do not yield the claimed critical initial and target spaces.

failure_location.quote:
The result is a direct consequence of \eqref{eq:parabolic_regularity_low} and
    \eqref{eq:parabolic_regularity_high} together with the complex interpolation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Formulate the corollary using Eθ=[H¹₀,H²₀]θ and Fθ=[H⁻²,H⁻¹]θ. At the critical index, use the matching interpolation, dual-test, and graph spaces in the subsequent assumptions and results.
issues.overall_effect: The θ=1/2 cases of interpolated regularity, parabolic Galerkin orthogonality, and the abstract error estimate are unsupported. The noncritical choices used for the stated C¹ and C⁰ applications are unaffected.
issues.title: Complex interpolation does not give the stated ordinary Sobolev spaces at the critical index
issues.why_classification: This requires a contained correction of the critical data and target spaces, rather than a new global argument; the concrete convergence orders and intended element families survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The truncated test controls only prefix dissipation and prefix jumps, not their full-time totals together with the largest nodal norm at the same unit initial-data coefficient. For a normalized single spatial eigenmode, f=0, and dG(0) on increasingly fine uniform time meshes, the claimed left side tends to 1+(1−e^(−2λT))/2>1, whereas the right side is 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Combine the full-interval and truncated estimates separately and place a uniform constant on the entire right-hand side, including the initial-data norm.
issues.overall_effect: The stated stability inequality is false with coefficient 1 on the initial-data term.
issues.title: The discrete stability theorem also loses a constant when introducing the nodal maximum
issues.why_classification: Only a routine constant adjustment is needed; the uniform stability guarantee and all parameter regimes remain unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Each of the local terms $\|\varphi_h\|_{H^{1+\theta}(T)}^2$ can be bounded by the corresponding
  term $\|\varphi_h\|_{H^{2}(T)}^2$ contained in $\vertiii{\varphi_h}_h^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The global fractional seminorm of the gradient contains interactions across element interfaces that the displayed right side omits. Even on a uniform shape-regular mesh, continuous piecewise affine functions with alternating nodal values of size h have a bounded sum of local H^(1+θ) norms, while their global squared H^(1+θ) norm grows like h^(−2θ). Such functions belong to the stated Lagrange spaces of degree at least two. Thus this argument does not establish the claimed mesh-uniform stability condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false localization by a discrete fractional-norm estimate controlled by the broken H² norm together with the h_e⁻¹-weighted normal-derivative jumps, and then use discrete Poincaré and interior-penalty coercivity.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed verification of the additional low-regularity stability hypothesis for C⁰ elements is invalid; the conditional theorem itself does not depend on this verification.
issues.title: The asserted fractional Sobolev norm localization omits cross-element contributions
issues.why_classification: Recovering the intended application requires a contained nontrivial discrete embedding or enrichment argument, but does not require changing the main error-analysis architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\theta = \frac12 - \varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon>0$ can be chosen arbitrarily small.

issues.failure_explanation: For the chosen θ, the defined graph space uses Aψ∈H^(−3/2+ε), consistently with the earlier H^(5/2+ε) regularity, not H^(5/2−ε). An arbitrary function in H^(5/2−ε) has second derivatives only in H^(1/2−ε), which need not possess the edge traces required by the displayed interior-penalty form. Consequently the asserted projection is not defined on all of the promised rough-input class.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\eta>0$ is a sufficiently large penalty constant.

issues.failure_explanation: No uniform shape-regularity or comparable geometric restriction is imposed on the mesh family. The spatial approximation and inverse-trace estimates invoked for the h² bound and a fixed penalty are not uniform on arbitrarily flat simplices. For example, a constant Hessian on a triangle has edge-to-volume squared norm ratio |e|/|T|, so the normalized trace factor |e|²/|T| can diverge independently of the maximum mesh size. The required uniform geometric premise is missing.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \jump{\frac{\pa v}{\pa n}} =-\frac{\pa v}{\pa n_e}\quad \text{and}\quad\avg{\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n^2}} = -\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n_e^2}.

issues.failure_explanation: For smooth clamped ψ, elementwise integration by parts leaves the boundary contribution ∫∂Ω ψ_nn ∂n v_h from the Hessian volume term. Because both the boundary jump and boundary average are defined with minus signs, the added consistency term contributes the same quantity rather than cancelling it. After interior-edge cancellation, a_h(ψ,v_h)=⟨Δ²ψ,v_h⟩+2∫∂Ω ψ_nn∂n v_h in general. Thus Assumption ass:discrete_bilin_form fails for the specified C⁰ construction.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: On boundary edges, define the average of the second normal derivative as +∂²v/∂n_e², while retaining the negative normal-derivative jump. The boundary terms then cancel.
issues.overall_effect: The application of the abstract error theorem and the cited Ritz estimate to the printed C⁰ method is invalid. The conforming method and the conditional abstract theorem are unaffected.

issues.why_classification: A local sign correction, checked by routine integration by parts, restores consistency without changing the intended method family or convergence guarantees.
